Request for Information (RFI)
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is posting these draft requirements (see attachments) and questions to obtain feedback from industry to help shape the next generation of contracts supporting the Superfund Remedial Program. EPA’s goal is to increase the performance-based aspects of the requirements, providing more flexibility to contractors in how work is performed while ensuring EPA receives the necessary services/deliverables. Contractors are welcome to make Track Changes within the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) and resubmit recommendations back to the agency for consideration. Additionally, EPA has included a list of questions below on specific topics for feedback. It is the Government’s intent to use the recommendations and feedback received from industry to help better inform the strategic direction of the procurement process (e.g. requirement refinement, improvement, or clarification), but is under no obligation to incorporate any proposed changes into the final PWS. All information and documentation posted under this notice is preliminary in nature and may be updated or amended prior to the release of the formal solicitation.
The agency intends to post draft solicitations for each requirement at a later date for industry questions and/or feedback. Additionally, EPA is developing an external-facing website to enable future posting of information and facilitate communication. It is EPA’s hope the website will be used not only to facilitate communication between EPA and industry regarding the next generation of contracts, but also be a useful resource for intra-industry communication for Prime/Sub relationship building. A future notification will be posted when the external website is operational.
This notice does not constitute a formal solicitation. Once a solicitation is posted, all responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by the agency.
Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay any cost incurred in response to this notice; all costs associated with responding to this notice will solely be at the interested parties’ expense. Any information provided by industry to the Government as a result of this notice is voluntary. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation(s).
The questions in this RFI are for market research and information-gathering purposes only. They do not reflect final agency requirements, preferences, or decisions, and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Agency to any particular acquisition strategy, scope, contract type, or solicitation content.
Basic information on the current Remedial Acquisition Framework (RAF) program and contracts is located at https://www.epa.gov/superfund/remedial-acquisition-framework.
EPA will not post any of the responses received for these questions. Only submissions made via FedConnect by the closing date/time are permitted. NO EMAILS. NO PHONE CALLS. NO OTHER SUBMISSION METHODS AUTHORIZED.
The Agency may use Super Intelligence (SI) tools to analyze or summarize industry responses; however, Government personnel will review all submissions and make all decisions.

QUESTIONS FOR INDUSTRY:
Topic 1: Geographic Structure & Competition
EPA is considering awarding multiple award contracts based upon four (4) geographic zones (Regions 1–3; 4+6; 5+7; 8–10) based on regional profiles and programmatic needs. Vendor pools may be limited per suite and per zone to ensure meaningful participation and reduce task order award cycle time.
1. If broken out into these four zones, what zone(s) would your firm compete for award?
2. How will this 4-zone structure impact your firm’s ability to staff, compete, and price work compared to the current 3-zone structure (1-3, 4-7, 8-10)?
3. If awarded a contract, would limiting the number of awards within each zone to five contracts increase your firm’s likelihood of competing for task orders (versus if the pool were larger)?
4. If you were awarded a contract, what contract structures, incentives, or support measures would encourage you to actively compete in all task orders for which you are qualified?
Topic 2: Contract Pricing Structure & Performance-Based Acquisition (PBA)
As demonstrated by the draft PWSs, EPA is exploring broader use of performance-based services and opportunities to leverage fixed-price components where tasks areas can be sufficiently defined.
1. Which, if any, task(s)/subtask(s) are suitable to fixed price?
2. How should EPA structure fixed priced units of measure (e.g., per meeting, per permit, per deliverable)?
3. Are the Results, Context, and Performance standards, as currently written within the draft PWSs, would improve your firm’s ability to execute the work?
4. What assumptions should EPA provide to enable accurate pricing on early stage tasks?
Topic 3: Discrete Investigation and Site Cleanup Operations (DISCO) Suite
The Agency is considering the addition of another suite of acquisition vehicles, DISCO, to provide rapid response services to support urgent, discrete, and short-term field needs (e.g., single sampling events, installing security fencing, etc.) with the goal of awarding competitively placed task orders within 30-calendar days. EPA acknowledges there is a substantial amount of overlap in scope between ESO and DISCO.
1. If offered, would your company compete for only DISCO, or would it compete for DISCO and ESO? Briefly explain why.
2. From industry’s perspective, what barriers in the current RAF suites make it difficult to compete for urgent task orders and to mobilize into the field after task order award?
3. Have you experienced other contract vehicles that accommodate a 30-calendar day award timeframe? What type of vehicle where they (BOA, BPA, IDIQ, SATOC)?
Topic 4: Permits & Access Agreements
1. How do you normally handle permit equivalence, infrequent permits, and routine site access agreements?
2. Which elements of permitting and access should EPA standardize vs. leave to regional discretion?
Topic 5: Data Validation Responsibilities
1. How should contractor responsibilities for regional lab/Contract Laboratory Program (CLP) data validation be scoped to avoid redundant cost?
2. Do you have any recommendations as to how the Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) development could be sped up or standardized to enable quicker deployment to sites?
Topic 6: General
1. Is there any other relevant, PWS related information not pertaining to acquisition award timeframe that you'd like share?
2. Do you have any concerns or recommendations on the use of super intelligence (SI) in the administration of the contracts (either by EPA or the contractor)?

For background, the subject acquisition is anticipated to provide support services for the “Technical Support for the Drinking Water Optimization Program.” The drinking water optimization program began in the late 1980’s with a focus on enhancement and implementation of the Drinking Water Composite Correction Program (CCP). Implementation of the CCP resulted in documented improvements on individual surface water treatment plant performance. The documented success of the CCP, its value for drinking water primacy programs and the desire to apply CCP principles more broadly resulted in the creation of an Area-wide Optimization Program (AWOP). Broad-scale public water system performance improvements and the resulting drinking water quality improvements have been achieved via AWOP implementation. Public Water System Supervision (PWSS) programs implement their AWOPs to enhance public health protection and to benefit from the resulting proactive assistance with regulatory compliance.
The AWOP was established with a focus on turbidity removal, resulting in greater protection against the risk of microbial pathogens passing through treatment plant processes. The program continues the focus on turbidity removal while expanding its technical scope to include optimization of both treatment plant and distribution system operations to minimize the formation of disinfection by-products (DBPs) and maintaining adequate disinfectant residual. The technical scope of the program also includes optimization of process control for ground water treatment and conveyance, and many unconventional (alternate) treatment processes. The program’s documented impact on enhancing public health protection has also been called upon to address other public health challenges such as treatment for cyanobacteria associated with harmful algal blooms and arsenic removal. The National AWOP has been structured to address additional public health challenges, depending on the commitment of resources to the program.

Authority
RFO 12.102(a) (decision to restrict competition, including brand-name without “equal,” at or below the SAT) and RFO 11.204(a) (brand-name requirement: essential, supported by market research, documented in the file, posted for acquisitions over $25,000).
2.
Acquisition and requirement
Commercial service, RFO 12.201-1: firm-fixed price under purchase order, 12-month base plus three 12-month options. The value of the acquisition, including all options, exceeds $25,000 (RFO 1.107(c)(1)). Service must be performed by Skalar, Inc. or a Skalar-authorized provider using genuine Skalar parts; no “equal” parts. The RFQ was posted publicly on September 22, 2026, so that any authorized provider could quote.
3.
Why the brand-name requirement is essential (RFO 11.204(a)(1))
•
Skalar support plans are governed by the Velaris Support and Maintenance Plans (2026). Section 7.1.1 voids coverage if the instrument is serviced by a non-authorized provider; section 7.1.5 requires genuine parts. Service from an unauthorized provider, or with non-genuine parts, would leave the Government without manufacturer coverage.
•
Formacs HT is a proprietary analyzer. Its service procedures, calibration routines and preventative-maintenance kits are specific to the instrument and available only through the manufacturer and its authorized network.
4.
Market research
The manufacturer and two other potential sources were considered: a national equipment-maintenance reseller that would place the work with the manufacturer and could not commit to the required site visits, and a third-party laboratory service firm with no established Skalar authorization or access to genuine parts. No source other than the manufacturer and its authorized providers was found. Details are in the market research report in the contract file.
5.
Posting and determination
Posted to SAM.gov on September 24, 2026, with notice 68HE0826Q0053 (RFO 11.204(a)(3)). Manufacturer or manufacturer-authorized service using genuine Skalar parts is essential to the Government’s requirement; market research shows that other companies’ similar services, and services lacking the feature, do not meet and cannot be modified to meet the agency’s minimum needs; and the requirement is limited to the extent necessary (RFO 11.102(a)(1)(ii). STATEMENT OF NEED
Kongsberg trawl sensors and associated deployment components
NOAA Ship REUBEN LASKER
140802-26-0605
1. Purpose
NOAA Ship Reuben Lasker requires a mission-critical spare suite of Kongsberg trawl sensors and associated deployment components for its installed Kongsberg trawl-monitoring system. The equipment will provide immediate onboard replacement capability when an operational sensor or deployment component fails.
2. Mission Need and Background
Reuben Lasker conducts fisheries surveys that depend on real-time trawl information to confirm net condition and performance, support safe fishing, and collect consistent scientific data. The existing sensor suite is operational, but the ship lacks sufficient onboard replacements for the critical components listed below.
A sensor failure at sea can interrupt sampling and place data quality and mission completion at risk. Compatible onboard spares allow immediate replacement, limit lost ship time, and avoid delays and added costs to transport specialized equipment during a survey.
Brand-name compatibility: Kongsberg components are required because they are spares for an installed Kongsberg trawl-monitoring system. Replacements must communicate with the existing equipment and software and use established deployment, charging, maintenance, and troubleshooting processes. This is a compatibility requirement, not a brand preference.

Summary.PSC / FSC: 7G22-IT AND TELECOM - NETWORK: SATELLITE AND RF COMMUNI
Summary.Contracting office: Social Security Administration Office of Acquisition and Grants 00000
Summary.Description: The SSA Security and Resilcilence group is moving away from hand held land mobile radio systems due to the cost of replacement. The HQ Campus and the National Support Center are in need of replacing thier existing LMR systems due to End of Life, End of Support & End of replacement parts. All FSL-IV facilities are required to provide a centrallized communications system for all guard forces, and the agency COOP plan requries a centralized agency level communications systems for emergency communications during emergency situations. SecRes has identified the most cost effective and resilient solution to be the federal FirstNet Commissions Priority Communications system. This system will provide better than 911 priority across all identified agency iphone/stand alone push to talk devices anywhere there is AT&T signal. However, the risk is that if the AT&T cellular network fails for any reason, the devices would not work. The devices in this SSASy will provide emergency satellite backlink to the FirstNet network, restoring signal for the identified facilities in less than 20min ensuring near immediate restoration to communications during emergency outages.
